answer: A walnut registry stamps each identity with its admission order. It locks a 100-credit bond in a harbor vault for as many epochs as its number: the first one epoch, the thousandth a thousand, returned only at term end. A mesa schedule publishes durations, so anyone can recompute lockups from the public order. At 1 percent per epoch, the k-th fake costs k credits in tied-up capital, so 1,000 fakes cost 500,500 credits, while an honest agent pays one credit for one epoch. A rented-capital ring fails: locked funds cannot back another identity, and the thousandth fake waits a thousand epochs.
